subject: Bluehaven - schedule working session for private/VPC architecture review
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Turner <emily@bluehaven.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@bluehaven.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bluehaven - schedule working session for private/VPC architecture review

Hi Emily / Samir —

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier — really helpful to understand Bluehaven's latency needs and data isolation requirements. As next step we'd like to run a 60–90 minute private/VPC architecture working session focused on:

- mapping a minimal network topology for a proof-of-concept (what subnets, NAT, peering, or transit would be needed)
- options for private control plane vs. customer-managed control plane
- data flow, keys, and audit/logging requirements (SOC2 questions)
- rough timeline and gating items for an on-prem or VPC-hosted rollout

Proposed windows (all times in PT / ET / UTC):
- Tue Apr 6, 10:00–11:30 PT / 13:00–14:30 ET / 17:00–18:30 UTC
- Wed Apr 7, 14:00–15:30 PT / 17:00–18:30 ET / 21:00–22:30 UTC
- Thu Apr 8, 08:00–09:30 PT / 11:00–12:30 ET / 15:00–16:30 UTC

Pre-call asks (helps us tailor the session):
1) a brief network/topology sketch (VPC CIDRs, whether you use transit gateway, any firewall appliances)
2) list of internal stakeholders to invite (security, infra, procurement)
3) any hard SLO/latency targets for the primary API endpoints

I attached our SOC2 summary and a short network checklist that most customers find useful. Monica (cc'd) will lead the session from our side; Lauren will handle calendar logistics.

If those slots don't work, tell us two alternatives and we'll accommodate. Looking forward — we'll keep this focused and technical.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (pdf)] [attachment: network-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: Emily Turner <emily@bluehaven.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@bluehaven.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bluehaven - schedule working session for private/VPC architecture review

Thanks Sean — very helpful recap. Samir (infra lead) and I can attend. A couple quick notes:

- We prefer Wed Apr 7 in the 14:00 PT window (the later window on Wed) — that looks like the best option for our engineers.
- We will need a short NDA and a copy of SOC2 evidence summary for our security review before any detailed connectivity discussion. Could you confirm what we can expect to receive?
- For scope: Samir will want to dive into service sidecar requirements (if any), whether a private control plane requires peering, and any firewall/NAT implications.

I attached a one-page topology sketch showing where our services live (very high-level).

Emily Turner
Director, Infrastructure & Security | Bluehaven AI
[attachment: bluehaven-topology-sketch.png (png)]

Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bluehaven - schedule working session for private/VPC architecture review

Emily — perfect, appreciate the sketch. Wed Apr 7 14:00 PT works for us; I’ll get that put on the calendar once Lauren confirms.

Regarding SOC2/NDA: attached is our two-page SOC2 summary and a short network checklist. For deeper SOC2 artifacts we have an NDA process — I’ve included a DocuSign MSA link in Lauren's note below. If you need something specific for your security intake form, send it over and Monica will coordinate with our compliance team.

Quick clarifications for the agenda so Samir can prepare:
- We do not require VPC-level access for the architecture review — we’ll review topology and network requirements at a high level. Any runtime access (for debugging) would be a later, gated step.
- We will demo a sample private deployment topology (diagram + traffic flow) and present three connectivity patterns: VPC peering, TGW, and VPN/DirectConnect hybrid.

Monica will run the technical portion; I'll kick off the call. If Samir can share a short list of questions he wants covered we’ll prioritize them.

Thanks,
Sean
